# Notion: Company Brief

**What they do:** Notion is a productivity software company that offers an all-in-one workspace platform combining note-taking, project management, wikis, databases, and collaboration tools into a single customizable interface, allowing users to build their own systems using flexible building blocks rather than rigid templates.

**Market:** They compete in the crowded productivity/collaboration software space against players like Asana, Airtable, Confluence, and Evernote, serving a broad range of customers from individual users and students to startups and large enterprises seeking to consolidate multiple tools into one platform.

**Notable facts:** Founded in 2013 by Ivan Zhao and Simon Last, Notion achieved a $10 billion valuation in 2021 and has grown primarily through strong product-led growth and viral word-of-mouth adoption, particularly among startups, creators, and tech-savvy professionals who use it to replace multiple disparate apps like Trello, Google Docs, and Evernote.

Stripe is a financial technology company that provides payment processing infrastructure and software, enabling businesses to accept payments online and manage financial operations through simple, developer-friendly APIs. It serves a massive global market ranging from small startups to large enterprises, including well-known companies like Amazon, Shopify, and Salesforce, and operates in dozens of countries worldwide. Founded in 2010 by Irish brothers Patrick and John Collison, Stripe has grown into one of the most valuable private companies in the world, with a valuation that has reached tens of billions of dollars, and has expanded beyond payments into areas like billing, fraud prevention, and business financing.

Figma is a cloud-based design platform primarily used for collaborative interface design, prototyping, and design systems management, enabling multiple team members to work on the same file simultaneously in real-time. The company serves the UI/UX design market, competing with tools like Adobe XD and Sketch, and has become a dominant player particularly among product design teams, startups, and enterprises due to its browser-based accessibility and collaborative features. Figma gained significant attention when Adobe announced plans to acquire it for approximately $20 billion in 2022, though the deal was ultimately abandoned in December 2023 due to regulatory pressure from antitrust authorities in the UK and EU.

# Airtable Brief

**What they do:** Airtable is a cloud-based platform that combines the simplicity of a spreadsheet with the power of a database, allowing users to organize, link, and visualize data through customizable tables, views (grid, kanban, calendar, gallery), and automation workflows—no coding required.

**Their market:** They target business teams across industries (marketing, product, operations, HR) who need flexible tools for project management, content planning, CRM, and workflow automation, competing with tools like Notion, Monday.com, and traditional database/spreadsheet software while serving both SMBs and enterprise clients like Netflix and Shopify.

**Notable facts:** Founded in 2012 by Howie Liu, Andrew Ofstad, and Emmett Nicholas, Airtable reached unicorn status and was valued at around $11 billion in its 2021 Series F funding round, and has increasingly integrated AI features to help users build custom apps and automate workflows directly within their bases.

# Linear: Company Brief

**What they do:** Linear builds a project management and issue-tracking tool designed specifically for software teams, emphasizing speed, keyboard-driven workflows, and a clean, minimalist interface that reduces the friction typically associated with tools like Jira.

**Their market:** They target software engineering and product teams at startups and tech companies, positioning themselves as the modern alternative for organizations that prioritize developer experience and want to move away from clunky, enterprise-heavy project management software.

**Notable facts:** Linear has gained a reputation for exceptional product design and performance (often cited as a benchmark for "fast" web apps), has been adopted by numerous high-profile startups and tech companies (including Vercel, Cash App, and Retool), and has raised significant venture funding while maintaining a strong cult-like following among developers for its opinionated, workflow-focused approach.

# Vercel: Company Brief

Vercel is a cloud platform company that provides infrastructure for building, deploying, and scaling web applications, with a particular focus on frontend development and serverless architecture. The company created and maintains **Next.js**, one of the most popular React frameworks used by developers worldwide, which has helped establish Vercel as a leading player in the modern web development and Jamstack ecosystem. Founded in 2015 by Guillermo Rauch (originally as Zeit), Vercel has grown into a major infrastructure provider trusted by companies like Nike, Under Armour, and Washington Post, and has raised significant venture funding at a valuation exceeding $3 billion, positioning itself as a key competitor to platforms like Netlify and AWS Amplify.

# Ramp: Company Brief

Ramp is a fintech company that provides corporate credit cards and spend management software designed to help businesses save time and money through automated expense tracking, bill payment, and financial operations tools. The company targets businesses of all sizes—from startups to enterprises—competing in the corporate card and spend management space against players like Brex and traditional providers like American Express. Notable for its rapid growth, Ramp has become one of the fastest-growing fintech startups in the U.S., achieving a multi-billion dollar valuation (reported north of $8 billion in recent funding rounds) while emphasizing a mission-driven approach centered on helping companies operate more efficiently and profitably.

# Retool: Company Brief

**What they do:** Retool is a software development platform that enables companies to quickly build internal business tools and applications using a low-code/drag-and-drop interface, combined with the flexibility to add custom code when needed.

**Their market:** They target businesses of all sizes—from startups to large enterprises—that need to build internal software (like admin panels, dashboards, and CRUD apps) faster than traditional development allows, appealing primarily to engineering and IT teams looking to reduce internal tooling overhead.

**Notable facts:** Founded in 2017 by David Hsu, Retool has grown rapidly and counts major companies like OpenAI, Amazon, DoorDash, and Brex among its customers; it reached a valuation of over $3 billion following a funding round led by top-tier VCs, reflecting strong investor confidence in the low-code enterprise tooling space.

Loom is a video messaging tool that lets users quickly record and share screen recordings, webcam videos, and audio for asynchronous communication, primarily targeting workplace collaboration, sales, customer support, and remote team communication. The company operates in the growing async communication and productivity software market, competing with tools that aim to reduce the need for live meetings and lengthy emails by enabling quick, personal video messages. Notably, Loom gained significant popularity during the remote work boom and was acquired by Atlassian in 2023 for approximately $975 million, integrating its video messaging capabilities into Atlassian's broader suite of collaboration tools like Jira and Confluence.

Webflow is a visual web development platform that allows designers and businesses to build, host, and launch responsive websites without writing code, using a drag-and-drop interface that generates clean HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The company competes in the website builder and no-code/low-code market, serving a range of customers from freelance designers and small businesses to marketing teams at larger enterprises who need custom-designed sites without heavy developer involvement. Founded in 2013 by Vlad Magdalin, Sergie Magdalin, and Bryant Chou, Webflow has raised significant venture funding (including a $140M Series B in 2019) and has positioned itself as a bridge between design flexibility and the ease of use typically associated with simpler site builders like Squarespace or Wix.
